observations.runtime_composition: The CLI now composes private Codex credential acquisition, deterministic selection, bounded failover, circuit breaking, separate loopback model/admin listeners, and sanitized admin state.
observations.multi_turn: A real persistent two-turn thread completed through the production router with one user-authorized account.
observations.historical_resume: After stopping and restarting both router and App Server on the same router port, thread/resume completed and retained the fixture context.
observations.cross_account_gate: The approved A-to-B M3.5 scenario remains mandatory and unrun because this device has one user-authorized Codex account.
observations.privacy: The E2E used an isolated private CODEX_HOME, fixture-only prompts, approvalPolicy never, a read-only sandbox, and persisted only booleans, terminal states, counts, and aliases.

blockers: A second distinct user-authorized Codex account is unavailable, so the required approved A-to-B E2E cannot run in this task.
residual_risks: Same-account App Server history rehydration does not prove that previous_response_id is portable to a replacement connection or another account.

Circuit-breaker persistence exists as a tested component but is not yet wired into runtime bootstrap lifecycle.
Codex auth.json or App Server protocol changes after the tested Codex CLI version may require a new authorized protocol capture.
